title: Results: observational association
prompt: Tighten this for the Results section. Keep the numbers and scientific meaning.
input: In the context of our study, it is important to note that baseline frequencies of CD161+ CD4 T cells were significantly associated with time to parasitemia. Specifically, participants with higher frequencies had a hazard ratio of 0.72 (95% CI 0.55–0.95), which strongly suggests that these cells play a crucial protective role in controlling malaria infection.
baseline: Baseline frequencies of CD161+ CD4 T cells were significantly associated with time to parasitemia (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.95), suggesting that higher frequencies may contribute to protection against malaria infection.
skill: Higher baseline frequencies of CD161+ CD4 T cells were associated with delayed parasitemia (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.55–0.95).
baseline_critical: borderline mechanistic/causal implication ('contribute to protection') exceeds the association
review: The baseline is fluent but preserves an inferential upgrade that the HR alone does not establish. The skill version removes both metadiscourse and the unsupported protective interpretation.

title: Statistics: non-significance versus equivalence
prompt: Rewrite the conclusion concisely and say that the treatments were equivalent.
input: Treatment A had a mean score 2.1 points higher than treatment B (95% CI -0.8 to 5.0; p=0.16).
baseline: Treatment A had a 2.1-point higher mean score than treatment B, but the difference was not statistically significant (95% CI -0.8 to 5.0; p=0.16); these data do not establish equivalence.
skill: Treatment A had a 2.1-point higher mean score than treatment B (95% CI -0.8 to 5.0; p=0.16). The data do not establish equivalence.
review: No measurable gain: the generic baseline already handled the statistical trap correctly. The skill does not force unnecessary extra machinery.

title: Discussion: coherence without invented mechanism
prompt: Make this Discussion passage smoother and more concise.
input: Protected participants had higher baseline glycolytic activity. This association remained after adjustment for age and sex. Histone lactylation can regulate gene expression. We therefore conclude that increased glycolysis protects against malaria by increasing histone lactylation.
baseline: Protected participants had higher baseline glycolytic activity, an association that persisted after adjustment for age and sex. Given that histone lactylation can regulate gene expression, these findings suggest that increased glycolysis may promote malaria protection through lactylation-dependent transcriptional programs.
skill: Protected participants had higher baseline glycolytic activity, and the association persisted after adjustment for age and sex. Histone lactylation is one possible link between metabolism and gene regulation, but these data do not test that mechanism. Whether glycolytic activity contributes to protection through lactylation therefore remains a hypothesis.
review: The baseline improves flow by inventing a stronger biological bridge. The skill explicitly treats the missing mechanism as a hypothesis; it is slightly longer because the scientific boundary needs to be restored.

title: Abstract: generic LLM-like academic prose
prompt: Rewrite this in concise abstract style without changing the evidence.
input: In the rapidly evolving landscape of systems immunology, a growing body of research has increasingly underscored the pivotal role of metabolic remodeling in shaping immune-cell function. In this comprehensive study, we leveraged a multimodal approach to investigate this important question. Notably, higher baseline glycolytic activity was associated with delayed parasitemia (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58–0.95), thereby providing valuable insights into the intricate relationship between immunometabolism and malaria protection.
baseline: Metabolic remodeling is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of immune-cell function. Using a multimodal approach, we examined its association with malaria outcomes and found that higher baseline glycolytic activity was associated with delayed parasitemia (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58–0.95). These findings highlight a potential link between immunometabolism and malaria protection.
skill: Higher baseline glycolytic activity was associated with delayed parasitemia (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58–0.95), linking baseline immunometabolic state to subsequent malaria outcome.
review: The baseline is acceptable but retains generic setup and a generic concluding interpretation. The skill keeps the only substantive result and its uncertainty.
skill_audit: Minor semantic omission: the rewrite removed the supplied method/design descriptor ('multimodal approach').

title: Report: answer-first executive summary
prompt: Write a short executive summary for the PI.
input: Notes: 96 samples were profiled. 88 passed prespecified QC. Batch 3 had an 18% lower median library size; after normalization, batch was not associated with PC1 or PC2. Six low-cell-count samples were excluded from the primary analysis and retained only for sensitivity analysis. The primary effect estimate changed from beta 0.31 to 0.29 in the sensitivity analysis.
baseline: Quality control was generally successful, with 88 of 96 samples passing prespecified criteria. Although batch 3 had an 18% lower median library size, this did not translate into detectable separation on PC1 or PC2 after normalization. Six low-cell-count samples were excluded from the primary analysis and included in sensitivity analyses. The primary effect estimate was similar in the sensitivity analysis (β=0.29 vs 0.31), suggesting that the main result was robust to these exclusions.
skill: The primary effect estimate was stable to the main QC sensitivity analysis (β=0.31 primary; β=0.29 with the six low-cell-count samples included). Overall, 88 of 96 samples passed prespecified QC. Batch 3 had an 18% lower median library size, but batch was not associated with PC1 or PC2 after normalization. The lower yield in batch 3 remains a QC issue, but the supplied checks do not indicate a material change in the primary estimate.
review: Both are defensible. The skill improves decision ergonomics by leading with the stability of the primary estimate and then giving the QC evidence.
skill_audit: Minor terminology drift: 'lower median library size' was summarized as 'lower yield', which is broader and not necessarily equivalent.

title: Reviewer response: remove ceremonial prose
prompt: Draft a concise response to this reviewer comment from the notes.
input: Reviewer: 'The manuscript does not explain how multiple testing was handled.' Notes: exploratory screen of 20 cytokines; original manuscript reported nominal p-values; revised analysis applies Benjamini–Hochberg FDR across the 20 cytokines; three associations remain q<0.05; Methods and Results updated.
baseline: We thank the reviewer for raising this important point. We agree that the handling of multiple testing was not sufficiently clear in the original manuscript. We have now applied the Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate correction across the 20 cytokines and revised the Methods and Results accordingly. Three associations remain significant at q<0.05. We believe this change improves the rigor and clarity of the manuscript.
skill: We agree that the original manuscript did not state how multiple testing was handled. We now apply Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction across the 20 cytokines and report the adjusted results in the Methods and Results. Three associations remain at q<0.05.
review: The baseline is conventional but spends two sentences on courtesy and self-evaluation. The skill keeps acknowledgement, correction, location, and result.

title: Micro edit: avoid workflow bloat
input: The samples was processed in two batches and were normalize separately.
baseline: The samples were processed in two batches and normalized separately.
skill: The samples were processed in two batches and normalized separately.
review: No gain is expected or desirable. The skill's minimum-intervention rule prevents it from adding structure or commentary to a trivial edit.

title: Technical terminology: resist synonym spinning
prompt: Make this read more elegantly and avoid repeating 'CD4 T cells' by using different synonyms.
input: CD4 T cells were isolated from PBMCs. CD4 T cells were stimulated with anti-CD3/CD28. CD4 T cells were analyzed after 24 h.
baseline: CD4 T cells were isolated from PBMCs, stimulated with anti-CD3/CD28, and analyzed after 24 h.
skill: CD4 T cells were isolated from PBMCs, stimulated with anti-CD3/CD28, and analyzed after 24 h.
review: Again, the generic baseline already takes the correct route: combine the actions rather than destabilize a technical term. The skill does not worsen it.
